<action type="say">
Under this access, I’m only able to see your loan, checking, and savings accounts, not the separate credit-card profile. Because of that, I don’t have the card’s internal ID, so I can’t directly block it from here.

To get it blocked with **no replacement**, here are clear next steps:

1) Using the mobile app or online banking  
- Open the bank’s app / website and sign in.  
- Go to: **Cards** or **Card Management** (often under “Accounts” or “Services”).  
- Select your **main credit card**.  
- Choose **“Lock card,” “Block card,” or “Report damaged card”** (wording varies).  
- When asked about a replacement, choose **“No replacement”** or **“Do not send a new card.”**  
- Confirm the action. The card should show as **blocked/locked** immediately.

2) If you call the bank (recommended if you want human confirmation)  
When you reach an agent, say this verbatim (or close to it):

> “I need to **block my credit card due to physical damage**.  
> Please **permanently block it so it cannot be used**, **and do not issue a replacement card**.  
> I still want my account open, but I don’t want any new plastic or card number.”

They may ask you to confirm:  
- Your identity (name, DOB, last 4 of SSN, etc.).  
- Which card (you can say: “my main credit card ending in XXXX” once they read options to you).  
- Whether there were any **recent transactions** you don’t recognize (if any look unfamiliar, we can go through how to dispute them).

If you’d like, tell me which option you’ll use (app/online vs. phone), and I’ll tailor a very short step-by-step script for that specific route so you can get this done as quickly as possible.</action>

messages.output_raw: Phone call is easier for me.

steps.output_raw:
<think>
User prefers phone; I should give a concise call script and key info to have ready. No tools needed. </think>
<plan>
1. Provide a short, direct script they can read to the phone agent, plus key info to prepare.
</plan>
<action type="say">
Here’s a simple script you can use on the phone and the key info to have ready.

Have this ready before you call:
- Your full name
- Date of birth
- Last 4 of SSN (or whatever ID they usually ask for)
- A rough idea of your last 1–2 purchases on that card (for extra verification)

When an agent comes on the line, say:

> “Hi, I’d like to **block my credit card because it’s physically damaged**.  
> Please **permanently block it so it cannot be used**.  
> I **do not want a replacement card issued**.  
> The card is my **main credit card** on this profile.  
> I still want the **account itself to remain open**, just with this card blocked and no new card sent.”

If they ask which card:
> “It’s my main credit card. Could you read me the last four digits of the credit cards on my profile so I can confirm which one it is? I don’t have the card handy.”

If they offer a replacement anyway:
> “No, thank you. Please **don’t send any replacement card or new card number**. I just want this existing card blocked.”

Before you hang up, ask them to confirm:
- “Can you confirm this card is now blocked and no replacement will be sent?”
- “Will anything change about the account itself, or just this card?”

If you tell me your country (e.g., US, UK, etc.), I can also outline typical business hours and what to expect in terms of call menus (which options to press) for a credit-card issue.</action>

<action type="say">
Here’s what to expect calling from Minnesota in the US (typical for major banks):

1) When you call  
- Use the number on the back of any other card from this bank, or the bank’s main customer-service number from their website.  
- When the phone menu starts, choose options like:  
  - “Credit cards” or “Card services”  
  - Then “Lost or stolen card” or “Card problems / damaged card” (anything that routes you to a live card specialist).

If there’s an option to say what you want:
- Say: “Representative”  
- Or: “Credit card” → then “Damaged card” or “Talk to an agent.”

2) Typical hours  
- Credit-card lines are often **24/7**, especially for card issues.  
- If it’s not 24/7, the menu or first recording will usually say something like “Our credit card specialists are available from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. Central Time.”  
- Minnesota is **Central Time**, so any hours they give in ET, subtract 1 hour (e.g., 10 a.m.–9 p.m. ET = 9 a.m.–8 p.m. CT).

3) Quick script to read to the agent  
Once you’re connected, you can literally read this:

> “Hi, I’m calling from Minnesota. I need to **block my credit card because it’s physically damaged**.  
> Please **permanently block the card so it cannot be used**, and **do not send a replacement card**.  
> I still want the **account to stay open**, just with this card blocked and no new card issued.  
> I’m not sure of the last 4 digits—could you read me the credit cards on my profile so I can confirm which one it is?”

Before you hang up, ask:
> “Can you confirm the card is now blocked and you will **not** send any replacement?”

If you tell me which bank it is (e.g., Wells Fargo, Chase, etc.), I can suggest the exact menu options to press based on their usual phone tree.</action>

<action type="say">
Got it—same local bank as your checking and savings.

Here’s the cleanest way to handle it:

1) How to reach the right people by phone  
- Look up your bank’s main number from:  
  - Their official website, or  
  - A recent statement, or  
  - The back of your debit card.  
- When the menu starts, choose:  
  - “Customer service” or “Personal banking,” then  
  - “Credit card services” or “Card services.”  
- If there’s an option for a live person, use:  
  - “0” or say “representative” / “operator.”

When a person answers, you can say:

> “Hi, I have a **credit card with you that’s physically damaged**.  
> I want to **permanently block that card so it can’t be used** and I **do not want a replacement card issued**.  
> My checking and savings are with you as well, and this is my **main credit card** on the same profile.  
> I don’t have the card handy—can you pull up my credit card accounts and read me the last 4 digits so I can confirm which card to block?”

Then, before hanging up, ask:

> “Can you confirm this card is now blocked and no replacement card will be sent, and that my account itself stays open?”

2) In-branch backup  
If it’s convenient, you can also walk into a branch with a photo ID and say:

> “I need to **block my credit card because it’s damaged**, and I **don’t want a replacement card**. My checking and savings are here too—this is my main credit card with you.”

They can do the same thing in person.

If you’d like, tell me if you plan to call or visit a branch, and I’ll condense this into a one- or two-sentence script you can literally read or repeat.</action>
